answers.answer: A clearing is ruled by the player with more total warriors plus buildings than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules; Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. Vagabond cannot rule and cannot prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: ‘warriors plus buildings’; ‘Tokens and pawns do not contribute’; ‘Eyrie rule a tie’; ‘Vagabond cannot rule’

answers.answer: A normal move takes a positive number of your warriors/pawns from a clearing along a linking path to an adjacent clearing. You must rule the origin, destination, or both, and recheck rule for each move. The same pieces may be moved repeatedly, including in multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly treats them as paths.
answers.evidence: Move (4.2): ‘any positive number’; ‘rule origin or destination or both’; ‘move the same pieces repeatedly’; ‘Rivers are not paths’

answers.answer: Battle sequence: (1) defender may play a matching ambush (bird wild); attacker may foil with a matching ambush. The defender's card is discarded; if foiled it deals no hits, otherwise it deals two immediate hits, then is discarded. If no attacking warriors/pawns remain, battle ends immediately. Ambush hits are not capped by defender warriors. (2) Resolve before-roll effects; attacker chooses order if both sides have effects. (3) Roll: higher die is attacker's hits, lower die defender's; ties give equal results; each side's rolled hits are capped by its own warriors, Alliance defense reverses the dice, and Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. (4) Resolve after-roll effects, attacker choosing order if both have effects. (5) Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors) and subtract ignored hits; if defender has no warriors, attacker gets one defenseless extra hit (Vagabond instead is defenseless with no undamaged swords). (6) Each side deals its counted hits; hit recipient chooses own removal order but must remove all warriors before buildings/tokens, and chooses order of its removal-triggered effects. Both sides deal hits even if warriors were removed after rolling. Removing an enemy building/token scores one VP each, regardless of side, including when defending and outside battle. Vagabond hits damage items.
answers.evidence: Battle (4.3), six listed steps; ‘all its warriors must be removed before its buildings/tokens’; ‘Whoever removes an enemy building/token scores one VP each’

answers.answer: Craft from hand when permitted by activating crafting pieces matching each crafting icon at bottom left; card suit is not its cost. Each icon costs one matching-piece activation. A crafting piece ordinarily activates only once per turn (Vagabond may reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers). An item card cannot be crafted if that item is absent from map supply. You cannot craft a persistent effect identical to one already in your play area.
answers.evidence: Craft (4.1): icons ‘completely define this crafting cost’; ‘Each crafting piece may activate only once per turn’; item requires supply; cannot craft identical persistent effect

answers.answer: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand into your play area; remove your score marker and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that matching suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Dominance: ‘In own Daylight at at least 10 VP’; suit conditions at ‘start of own Birdsong’; ‘Cannot remove/replace activated card’

answers.answer: A dominance card spent for suit goes to the area near the map as available instead of the discard pile. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. A bird dominance remains bird, so its payment must be a bird card; a bird hand card may pay for a non-bird dominance. Taking it does not activate it, and neither taking nor activating uses a faction action allowance.
answers.evidence: ‘Whenever one would enter discard, put it near map available’; ‘spend matching card to take’; ‘Available bird dominance remains bird’

answers.answer: In a two-player game remove all four dominance cards, then shuffle the shared deck and deal three cards to each player. Cover four R building slots with ruins. The separate map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, and 2 coins; keep the four R-marked ruin items separate. Only Vagabond setup hides one R-marked bag, boot, hammer, and sword under one each of the four ruins; without Vagabond ruins have no items. Put map-supply items on their corresponding spaces. Set up factions in Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond letter order; this is distinct from turn order.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–7; ‘With two players, remove all four dominance cards’; ‘each player draws three cards’; faction setup order stated distinct from turn order

answers.answer: Only Marquise may place pieces in its Keep clearing; other players may move pieces into it. When any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this can happen outside battle. Hospitals have no destination if the Keep is absent. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.
answers.evidence: Keep: ‘Only Marquise may place’; Field Hospitals condition and matching card; ‘keep cannot be placed again if removed’

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight starts by crafting with workshops, then permits up to three actions plus one for each bird card spent outside an action, in any order/number except Recruit's limit. March is one compound action of up to two moves and cannot be interrupted between moves to spend a bird or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and is allowed only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise Daylight: ‘First craft’; ‘up to three actions, plus one per bird card’; March and Recruit procedures; Overwork cost

answers.answer: To build, choose a clearing Marquise rules with an open slot and a building type. Take that type's leftmost building from its track. Pay the full column cost by removing wood from the chosen clearing or from other ruled clearings connected to it by an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP on the uncovered track space. Building is not legal without the full cost, building piece, and open slot.
answers.evidence: Marquise Build: rule/open slot; leftmost building; wood from target or linked chain of ruled clearings; score exposed VP

answers.answer: Eyrie Birdsong: first Emergency Orders (if hand empty, draw one); second add one or two hand cards to Decree, no more than one bird card, in any columns; third New Roost. If no roosts remain on map, place a roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can legally be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Birdsong numbered steps; New Roost says fewest warriors ‘where all these pieces can be placed’

answers.answer: Eyrie crafts with roosts first, then resolves all Decree cards by columns in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order; cards within a column may be ordered freely and bird is wild. Recruit must place at a roost in a clearing matching that card (two warriors there with Charismatic). Move must move at least one warrior from a matching clearing and obey ordinary movement rules. Battle must begin in a matching clearing containing Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build must place a roost in a matching clearing Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, Turmoil begins immediately; the card cannot be skipped and later columns cannot be continued.
answers.evidence: ‘Craft using roosts first’; Decree column order; action-specific requirements; incomplete action triggers Turmoil

answers.answer: Turmoil: lose one VP for every bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none, flip all leaders face up before choosing); retuck Viziers into the new leader's columns. Daylight ends, but the normal Evening still occurs: score the roost track, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, and discard to five. Turmoil does not remove Eyrie warriors or buildings from the map.
answers.evidence: Turmoil steps and ‘End Daylight and proceed to the full normal Evening’; ‘does not remove your map warriors or buildings’

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one hand card matching the clearing (birds count) per affected move, not per warrior. If no matching card including birds is held, show the hand to Alliance, then Alliance draws one deck card into Supporters. If Supporters is full, discard the incoming card; the card payment or no-match draw still occurs.
answers.evidence: Outrage trigger, card payment per move, no-match hand reveal/draw, and full-stack discard are specified

answers.answer: Revolts must all be completed before any Spread Sympathy starts; after spreading begins you cannot return to Revolt that Birdsong. Revolt chooses a sympathetic clearing with no base and a base matching one still on Alliance board; spend two matching supporters. Remove all enemy pieces there, score one VP per enemy building/token removed, place the matching base, and place warriors equal to sympathetic clearings of that base's printed suit (including the revolt clearing) plus one officer. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to existing sympathy, or any clearing if none exists; spend the supporters shown above its next token, plus one matching supporter if one other player has at least three warriors there (Martial Law). Place token and score uncovered VP. It is impossible to use sympathy spread in this Birdsong to enable a later Revolt in that same Birdsong.
answers.evidence: Alliance Birdsong specifies complete all Revolts before Spread Sympathy; separate eligibility, supporter costs, Martial Law and results

answers.answer: Train during Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with an Alliance base to place one supply warrior in Officers; Supporters cannot pay. In Evening, Organize is one officer-enabled operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, place sympathy there, and score its uncovered VP; it has no supporter, adjacency, or Martial Law cost but requires legal token placement. Whenever a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing including birds and remove half the officers rounded up; if no bases remain, discard supporters in excess of five.
answers.evidence: Train, Organize, and Losing a base procedures stated

answers.answer: In Birdsong, Refresh flips two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed now gives no bonus. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, including into hostile warriors, and ignores effects preventing movement out. Vagabond Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra if the destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; normal Move ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. Slip is the free-boot exception. In Evening, if in a forest Rest returns damaged items to Satchel face up and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able; it does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Birdsong, Daylight Move, and four Evening steps

answers.answer: Explore: exhaust a torch in a ruin's clearing; take one hidden item face up into Satchel or its track and score one VP if an item was taken. Removing the last ruin item frees the building slot. Quest: in a matching clearing choose a face-up quest, exhaust its two listed items, put it in play as completed, choose either VP equal to completed quests of that matching type including this one or draw two cards, and draw a replacement quest; no card pays the quest. Repair: exhaust a hammer and move one damaged item to Satchel retaining its current face; ready tea/coins/bags go to tracks if space.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Explore, Quest, Repair procedures

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes it Hostile (except the special allied-warrior battle-loss rule). During battle on Vagabond's own turn, Infamy scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; hostile buildings/tokens therefore normally give two VP each (one removal VP plus Infamy). A hostile warrior gives one Infamy unless it is the one that first caused Hostility. Infamy is based on whose turn it is, not attacking side; there is none on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot undo Hostility, though Vagabond may still take a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another faction piece instead; Strike is not battle and yields no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Relationships: Hostile, Infamy, Aid, and Strike rules

answers.answer: Vagabond coalition is available only in a game with four or more players, in Vagabond's own Daylight at 10 or more VP. Choose a player not already in a coalition whose VP is lowest among the other players; choose among ties. Activate dominance, place your score marker on that player's faction board, and stop scoring. If the partner wins, Vagabond wins too, including through dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies and coalition does not grant Allied relationship powers. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent.
answers.evidence: Vagabond coalition paragraph specifies eligibility, timing, selection and consequences

answers.answer: A card overrides the Law; the Law overrides Learning to Play. Apply general and faction rules together where possible, and faction rule wins if incompatible. ‘Cannot’ is absolute unless explicitly overridden; the summary does not say an ordinary card can override a cannot automatically, so absent an explicit override it cannot.
answers.evidence: Precedence: ‘Card overrides Law; Law overrides Learning to Play’; ‘Cannot is absolute unless explicitly overridden’

answers.answer: If simultaneous effects have no clear order or decision maker, the player taking the turn chooses. In battle, the attacker chooses the order of same-timing before-roll/after-roll effects when both players have them. A Marquise March's two moves are one compound action; it cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: player taking turn chooses unclear simultaneous effects; March is compound and cannot be interrupted

answers.answer: ‘At start’ effects happen before all other effects in that phase; ‘at end’ effects happen after everything else in that phase and before the next phase. Once the last step of a turn begins, no other actions are allowed except actions explicitly permitted at end of Evening/turn; thus ordinary Daylight actions cannot be taken after beginning the last step.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure timing and last-step restriction

answers.answer: Hand size is public but contents are private; show/reveal contents only when explicitly instructed. Face-up piles may be searched or inspected; the deck cannot be inspected. Agreements are non-binding, cards may be transferred only as instructed, and actions require no consent.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Cards and hand information; ‘Agreements are non-binding’

answers.answer: When the shared deck empties, immediately shuffle the discard pile into a new deck. Birds substitute for any non-bird suit, including multiple cards of the same suit. If ordered to give or discard a non-bird suit, birds must be treated as that suit, with quantity determined by the instruction. A non-bird card cannot substitute when bird is explicitly required.
answers.evidence: Cards: immediate discard reshuffle; birds substitute rules and explicit bird exception

answers.answer: When an instruction cannot place, take, or remove all prompted pieces, place/take/remove the maximum possible; you cannot voluntarily do less. No proxies are allowed because pieces are finite. A shortage does not waive costs or prerequisites, and it does not waive Eyrie's obligation to complete Decree actions.
answers.evidence: Pieces finite, ‘no proxies’; maximum possible rule; does not waive costs/prerequisites or Eyrie Decree obligations

answers.answer: Pieces placed normally come from supply or the leftmost track space; removed faction pieces normally return to supply or the rightmost track space. Items removed from the game are permanently removed. For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects.
answers.evidence: Removed pieces and placement rules; ‘For simultaneous removal, remove all pieces before triggering removal effects’

answers.answer: Resolve forced actions as if the affected player chose them, retaining that player's abilities and restrictions. A player forced to battle makes its own battle decisions.
answers.evidence: Force: resolve as if affected player chose, retaining abilities/restrictions; forced player makes battle decisions

answers.answer: No. Replace requires both removal and placement to be possible, and the Keep's placement ban cannot be bypassed by replacing an enemy piece. Swap is distinct: swap ignores move/place restrictions, whereas a move/place follows its own restrictions.
answers.evidence: Place/remove/replace: Keep ban and ‘Swap ignores move/place restrictions’

answers.answer: Among players simultaneously reaching 30 VP, the tied player closest clockwise to the current player wins; this includes the current player.
answers.evidence: 30 VP: ‘tied player closest clockwise to current player wins, including current player’

answers.answer: Forests are adjacent to clearings touching them without crossing a printed path and to forests separated by just one printed path; on Winter, the river also divides forests. Vagabond Slip uses this forest adjacency rule, so Winter's river affects adjacency. Fall has no special rules.
answers.evidence: Forest adjacency definition; Winter river divides forests; Fall has no special rules

answers.answer: Marquise supplies 25 warriors and 8 wood. Put the Keep in any corner as its starting clearing. Put one warrior in every clearing except the diagonally opposite corner. Place one sawmill, workshop, and recruiter among the Keep clearing and adjacent clearings in any combination respecting slots. Put the remaining five buildings of each type on their tracks from right to left, leaving the leftmost space empty.
answers.evidence: Marquise setup (6.3)

answers.answer: Eyrie supplies 20 warriors. Place one roost and six warriors in a corner that is not another player's starting corner, diagonally opposite a starting corner if possible. Choose a leader and keep the others face up nearby; tuck the two bird Loyal Viziers into the columns listed for that leader. Fill the roost track with the other six roosts from right to left.
answers.evidence: Eyrie setup (7.3)

answers.answer: Alliance supplies 10 warriors, places its three bases in matching board spaces, and places ten sympathy on its track. It draws three additional cards face down into Supporters, separate from its three-card hand. It starts with no map pieces and no officers.
answers.evidence: Alliance setup (8.3)

answers.answer: Choose Thief, Tinker, or Ranger and place the pawn in any forest. Shuffle quests and display three face up. Take the character's S-marked starting items: tea, coins, and bags go face up on matching tracks, while other items go face up in Satchel; return unused S items to the box. Set every other faction's relationship marker to Indifferent. The R-marked ruin-item setup is outside this question and is described separately in the summary.
answers.evidence: Vagabond setup (9.3)

answers.answer: Recommended reach totals are at least 17 for two players, 18 for three, and 21 for four. Base reach values are Marquise 10, Eyrie 7, Vagabond 5, and Alliance 3. The Law allows adventurous groups to use any mix totaling at least 17.
answers.evidence: Recommended faction mix (5.2)

answers.answer: In Birdsong Marquise places one wood at each sawmill, one per sawmill even if multiple sawmills share a clearing, limited by the eight-wood supply. In Evening draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.
answers.evidence: Marquise Birdsong wood production and Evening draw

answers.answer: Recruit is once per turn and normally places one warrior at each recruiter. If supply cannot fill them all, place the maximum available warriors and choose among eligible recruiters where they go.
answers.evidence: Recruit: ‘If supply cannot fill all recruiters, place maximum available, choosing among eligible recruiters’

answers.answer: Eyrie crafted items score one VP instead of the printed VP under Disdain for Trade. Builder ignores Disdain, so Builder gets the printed item VP. Other extra crafting-point effects still apply even when Disdain applies.
answers.evidence: Disdain for Trade and Builder clauses

answers.answer: Builder has Viziers in Recruit and Move and ignores Disdain for Trade. Charismatic has Recruit and Battle Viziers; each Recruit places two warriors instead of one. Commander has Move and Battle Viziers and gets one extra hit as attacker. Despot has Move and Build Viziers; when removing at least one enemy building/token in battle, score one extra VP in addition to normal removal points.
answers.evidence: Eyrie leader table

answers.answer: No. Charismatic Recruit requires two warriors at the chosen roost; if only one remains, the required action cannot be fully completed and Eyrie immediately enters Turmoil. The maximum-placement shortage rule does not waive Eyrie's Decree obligations.
answers.evidence: Charismatic Recruit places two; incomplete Decree action causes Turmoil; shortage rule does not waive obligations

answers.answer: No. Alliance Guerrilla War reverses which die each side uses when Alliance defends: Alliance uses the higher die and attacker the lower. Warrior caps still apply.
answers.evidence: Guerrilla War: Alliance uses higher die and attacker lower; warrior caps still apply

answers.answer: Alliance cannot craft from Supporters; it crafts from hand with sympathy. Supporters are inspectable by Alliance, are spent only for suit, do not count as hand cards or toward hand limit. Without bases, the stack is capped at five; with any base it is unlimited.
answers.evidence: Supporters: separate face-down stack inspectable by Alliance, spent only for suit; Alliance Daylight crafts from hand

answers.answer: No. Alliance must finish all Revolts before beginning Spread Sympathy, and cannot return to Revolt after spreading begins. A sympathy token placed in that Birdsong therefore cannot enable a Revolt later in the same Birdsong.
answers.evidence: ‘Complete all Revolts before starting any Spread Sympathy’; newly spread sympathy cannot support same-Birdsong Revolt

answers.answer: No. Martial Law requires at least three warriors of one other player in the chosen clearing; two enemy players with two warriors each do not meet it. Martial Law increases Spread Sympathy's supporter cost by one, but it does not increase Organize's cost; Organize has no Martial Law cost.
answers.evidence: Martial Law counts three warriors of one other player; Organize has no Martial Law cost

answers.answer: Placing warriors in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger Outrage; moving any warriors into one does. Moving only the Vagabond pawn does not trigger it. If Allied warriors accompany Vagabond into sympathy, their movement does trigger Outrage because warriors moved into the sympathetic clearing; the card payment is per affected move, not per warrior.
answers.evidence: Outrage: triggers on moving any warriors; placing warriors and moving only Vagabond pawn do not; allied warriors moving into sympathy triggers

answers.answer: Alliance may take Move, Battle, Recruit, or Organize operations, in any order and repetition, up to its number of officers. Taking an operation does not consume an officer; officers stay on the board. After operations, draw one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus, then discard to five.
answers.evidence: Alliance Evening operations table and following draw instruction

answers.answer: The Vagabond pawn cannot be removed. When an enemy effect removes all enemy pieces from its clearing, instead of removing the pawn the Vagabond damages three items. A revolt specifically notes this result for the enemy Vagabond.
answers.evidence: Pawn and items: pawn cannot be removed; remove-all effect instead damages three items; Revolt repeats exception

answers.answer: Vagabond's rolled-hit cap as attacker or defender is the number of all undamaged swords in Satchel, whether face up or face down; exhausted undamaged swords count. As defender Vagabond is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. Vagabond takes hits as item damage: one hit damages one undamaged item of its choice, and excess hits are ignored if no undamaged items remain.
answers.evidence: Vagabond Battle and Pawn/items rules

answers.answer: Face-up tea, coins, and bags in Satchel immediately move to an empty corresponding track space if possible; each track holds at most three of its type. Exhausting an item on a track sends it to Satchel. Track items do not count toward Satchel load. Damaged items cannot pay for actions even if face up; action costs require face-up undamaged items.
answers.evidence: Pawn and items track rules; damaged items cannot pay actions

answers.answer: Vagabond load is six items plus two per face-up bag on its track. Count items in Satchel and Damaged box together; track items do not count. Check capacity as the last Evening step, not immediately when acquiring items. Permanently remove chosen Satchel/Damaged items until within limit.
answers.evidence: Evening capacity step

answers.answer: Forest Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. In a forest it returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, and moves ready tea/coins/bags to tracks if able. Refresh flips exhausted items face up during Birdsong; Repair exhausts a hammer to move one damaged item to Satchel while keeping its face, with ready tea/coins/bags moved to tracks if space.
answers.evidence: Rest explicitly does not refresh undamaged exhausted items; Refresh and Repair procedures

answers.answer: Aid exhausts any one item and gives a card matching the clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even if Hostile. A crafted item is not required to perform Aid; Vagabond may take one from the recipient's Crafted Items box if available, but no item is required to Aid. To advance a non-Hostile relationship one space, Aid that faction the number of times printed between the current and next spaces in the same turn; each Aid counts for only one improvement. At Allied, further Aid scores two VP each.
answers.evidence: Aid action and Relationships improvement rules

answers.answer: At Allied status, each subsequent Aid scores two VP. Vagabond may move warriors of one Allied faction with the pawn into a clearing, but they follow their own movement restrictions including rule and Eyrie tie advantage; they cannot accompany a move specified to be alone. At start of battle as attacker, Vagabond may use warriors of one Allied faction against a different enemy, but may not use that ally's warriors to attack the ally itself.
answers.evidence: Relationships: Move with ally and Attack with ally

answers.answer: When using Allied warriors as its battle force against a different enemy, if Vagabond removes more of those allied warriors as hits than items it damages in that battle, that ally becomes Hostile at battle end. Equal numbers do not trigger it. This is a special battle-loss timing exception and is not about attacking the ally.
answers.evidence: Attack with ally: ‘more allied warriors than items you damage’; Hostile at battle end; equal numbers do not trigger

answers.answer: No, one clearing cannot satisfy mixed fox and rabbit crafting icons: the clearing must match all icons. The Vagabond pawn may be activated repeatedly for crafting by exhausting more hammers, despite the ordinary once-per-turn limit on each crafting piece. A crafted item may immediately be taken face up into Satchel or its track, provided the item is in supply.
answers.evidence: Craft: pawn may activate repeatedly; clearing must match all icons; crafted item immediately taken face up

answers.answer: Thief starts with boot, torch, tea, sword; Steal exhausts torch to take a random hand card from a player with faction pieces in the clearing. Tinker starts with boot, torch, bag, hammer; Day Labor exhausts torch to take a discard-pile card matching the clearing (bird always qualifies). Ranger starts with boot, torch, crossbow, sword; Hideout exhausts torch to repair three items while keeping their faces, immediately ending Daylight and beginning Evening.
answers.evidence: Base character table

answers.answer: When Explore takes the last item from a ruin, remove the ruin and free its building slot. Ordinary building placement does not remove a ruin; ruins can be removed only when explicitly allowed.
answers.evidence: Explore removes ruin when last item taken; ruins ‘can be removed only when explicitly allowed’

answers.answer: Coalition partners are not enemies, so they cannot be attacked as enemies under the ordinary battle rule. Coalition does not itself grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Coalition: ‘Coalition partners are not enemies’; ‘does not by itself grant Allied relationship powers’

answers.answer: The summary does not specify whether the two warriors are removed before or after the building in this scenario. If the first removed warrior makes the faction Hostile, that warrior gives no Infamy and the second hostile warrior gives one Infamy VP. The subsequently removed hostile building gives its normal one removal VP plus one Infamy VP, for two. Under that stated order the total is three VP; the summary makes the exception dependent on which warrior first causes Hostility.
answers.evidence: Infamy excludes ‘warrior that first made faction Hostile’; hostile building/token normally scores two VP

answers.answer: Hostile buildings alone do not require an extra boot: one boot pays for a normal Vagabond move. If the destination has hostile warriors, pay one extra boot beyond the normal one. The rule says any warriors of any Hostile faction, so several hostile factions' warriors still create the same one extra boot, not one extra per faction.
answers.evidence: Move: ‘one extra boot if destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction’; ‘not merely buildings/tokens’

answers.answer: No. Taking an available dominance card puts it into hand; it does not activate it. Taking and activating are separate Daylight choices, and neither uses a Marquise action allowance (nor a faction action allowance).
answers.evidence: Dominance: taking and activation are separate; neither requires a faction action allowance

answers.answer: Faction-piece ownership cannot change: a player owns the faction selected in setup and its listed faction pieces, except items. Items are not faction pieces or enemy pieces, and possessing an item does not make it faction-owned.
answers.evidence: Components: ‘Faction-piece ownership cannot change’; items excluded

answers.answer: An immediate-effect crafting card is resolved and discarded. An item card requires the item in map supply; take it from supply into Crafted Items and score listed VP, subject to Eyrie's exception. A persistent-effect card is kept in the play area and its effect applies; an identical persistent effect cannot be crafted if already there. A card in play is outside the hand and cannot be spent, discarded, or used for another purpose unless explicitly instructed.
answers.evidence: Craft: Immediate effect and Persistent effect clauses

answers.answer: Ambush cards cannot be crafted; a defender may play one for two immediate hits or attacker may play one to foil a defending ambush, matching the clearing. Dominance cards cannot be crafted; activate one to change victory condition or spend it for suit.
answers.evidence: Craft: Ambush and Dominance cards cannot be crafted and permitted uses listed

answers.answer: Choose factions and randomly determine starting player and seating; take faction boards and listed pieces and choose Fall or Winter. Put score markers at zero. Set battle dice nearby (the summary does not specify a required exact position). Factions set up in Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond letter order, which is distinct from turn order.
answers.evidence: Standard Setup steps 1, 2, 6, and 7

answers.answer: The first player to 30 VP wins immediately, on any player's turn; the player does not need to finish the action, phase, or turn first.
answers.evidence: 30 VP: ‘First to 30 wins immediately, on any player's turn’

answers.answer: To initiate battle, choose a clearing where you have warriors or a Vagabond pawn and an enemy is present, as defender. You do not need to rule the clearing.
answers.evidence: Battle: choose clearing with your warriors or pawn and an enemy; ‘does not require you to rule’

answers.answer: For same-timing before-roll or after-roll effects affecting both sides, the attacker chooses their order. The side taking hits chooses the order of effects triggered by removal of its own pieces.
answers.evidence: Battle steps 2, 4, and 6

answers.answer: In Count Hits, add extra hits (which are not capped by warriors), then subtract hits that are ignored.
answers.evidence: Battle step 5: ‘Add extra hits (uncapped by warriors), subtract ignored hits’

answers.answer: A non-Vagabond faction crafting an item takes it from the map item supply into its Crafted Items box and scores the VP listed on the card, except Eyrie's Disdain for Trade; crafted items are not exhausted for use as Vagabond does.
answers.evidence: Immediate effect item-card procedure; ordinary factions do not exhaust crafted items as Vagabond does

answers.answer: Eyrie activates roosts and Alliance activates sympathy as crafting pieces. A crafting piece's suit is the suit of its clearing. A three-color question-mark icon accepts any suit.
answers.evidence: Crafting piece faction list and suit; three-color question mark accepts any suit

answers.answer: Mobilize adds a card from Alliance's hand to Supporters, respecting the Supporters cap. During Daylight Alliance may craft, Mobilize, and Train in any order and any number, so it need not finish crafting before Mobilizing or Training.
answers.evidence: Alliance Daylight: Craft/Mobilize/Train in any order and number; Mobilize procedure

answers.answer: In ordinary Evening, Eyrie scores the VP shown on the rightmost empty roost-track space, then draws one card plus one per uncovered draw bonus and discards down to five. This same full Evening, including scoring and drawing, occurs after Turmoil.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Evening and Turmoil both specify roost score, draw, discard

answers.answer: Vagabond exhausts one sword to initiate its Daylight Battle action. An exhausted (face-down) but undamaged sword cannot pay the cost because actions require exhausting a face-up undamaged item; it can still count toward rolled-hit cap because all undamaged swords in Satchel count whether face up or face down.
answers.evidence: Battle exhausts one sword; hit cap includes face-up or face-down undamaged swords; action payment requires face-up undamaged item

answers.answer: A turn proceeds Birdsong, then Daylight, then Evening. Turns go clockwise, so after Evening the next player clockwise takes their turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: clockwise, Birdsong → Daylight → Evening

answers.answer: For each hit, Vagabond chooses one undamaged item to damage; it goes to the Damaged box without changing whether its face is up or down. Already-damaged items cannot absorb another hit. If no undamaged items remain, excess hits are ignored.
answers.evidence: Pawn and items: one hit damages one undamaged item of choice; damage does not change face; excess hits ignored when none remain
